title: Bending a Public MCP Server Without Breaking It — Nimrod Hauser, Baz
talk_summary: Nimrod Hauser shows how a generic third-party MCP server (Playwright) degraded an agentic spec-reviewer, then walks through five fixes: curating tools, rewriting descriptions, deterministic guardrails, composing new tools from existing ones, and calling tools as plain functions outside the agent loop. The baseline run failed with a hallucinated URL and bad screenshot; after the fixes it passed with correct evidence.

takeaways.technique: Curate the tool list per agent role
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of exposing all 21 Playwright tools, they filter out tools the use case never needs (resize, drag, run code in browser), cutting context and choice space.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of 21 tools which we used to have, I expect to see less. And so we have 16

takeaways.what_they_do: They wrap each upstream tool in a thin shim that keeps the same implementation but swaps in a longer, opinionated description telling the agent ordering rules and tool preferences.
takeaways.evidence_quote: before calling hover before calling click please use this tool before. So we can kind of really affect its behavior

takeaways.what_they_do: Before invoking a sensitive tool, they validate arguments with plain code (e.g. screenshot path must be under the screenshots dir); on violation they raise an agent-facing error message instead of failing the run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if it is not a valid path, it will not reach invocation. It will raise an error

takeaways.technique: Compose purpose-specific tools from existing ones
takeaways.what_they_do: They add an 'evidence screenshot' tool that reuses the screenshot implementation but has its own description and naming convention (include ticket number), so the agent picks it in the right context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we created a new agent called the evidence tool

takeaways.technique: Take deterministic steps out of the agent loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Login is done by plain code (inject JWT into local storage, click login) before the agent starts, because it is always required and the agent did it poorly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: There is no agentic flow for spec reviewer that does not begin with a login

takeaways.technique: Baseline-then-iterate on tool config with a fixed eval case
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep a toy spec-reviewer with a known ticket+design and rerun it after each tool change, comparing verdict and evidence (v0 failed with hallucinated URL, final passed).
